rationale: The Latin anchor *jus Quiritum* ("the law/right of the Quirites/Roman citizens") firmly places this in the context of the ancient Roman Empire and its citizenship, ruling out any modern sense. The Old English compound Róm-wealh (Rome-foreigner/Roman) and the attestations in early medieval texts (Widsith, Exeter Book) likewise refer to inhabitants of the ancient Roman world, matching roman.n.02 precisely.
